newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks move sideways in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks move sideways in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks trended mostly sideways in early trade on Tuesday morning after modestly easing at the open as institutions took profits on some of the weaker blue chips, brokers said.
"This is just a bout of normal profit taking," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The Hang Seng was down 0.71 points at 12,103.57 after about half an hour of trade, off an early low of 12,132.36. Turnover was a robust HK$1.2 billion.
"But there is very little selling," said another broker with a local house.
Brokers said that they were seeing an increase in retail and regional fund interest in the Hong Kong market.
Vickers' Mak also said institutions were switching funds to Hong Kong from elsewhere. "That's why (performances in) Asian markets are so mixed," he said
The local broker said recent selling in Bangkok of even first-tier blue chips should free more funds for Hong Kong.

But brokers said that while big-cap blue chips in the property sector were still being sought by investors and there was very little selling pressure, they expected to see some consolidation in the next couple of days.
The finance sector was leading the market in early trade, while the commercial and industrial sector and H shares brought up the rear.
HSBC continued its strong performance, gaining HK$0.50 to HK$147.00. The share has been leading the market for most of 1996.
The share broke through its long term resistance level at HK$128.00 on August 5 and with only one brief pullback has advanced quite strongly since then, said one local technical analyst.
Subsidiary Hang Seng Bank was holding steady at HK$86.00, after briefly touching another all time high at HK$86.25.
Property stocks remained firm despite recent gains. Cheung Kong led the sector with a gain of HK$0.75 to HK$61.50, while Henderson Land advanced HK$0.25 to HK$68.25.
Brokers said red chips and H share were volative. CITIC Pacific continued its strong run, adding HK$0.30 to HK$36.90, a new high. Guangdong Investment was unchanged at HK$5.90.
Among the H shares, Shanghai Petrochemical eased HK$0.05 to HK$2.20, while Qingling Motors rose HK$0.05 to HK$3.25.
